newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rises as El Nino scare strikes.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rises as El Nino scare strikes.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat futures continued to firm on Wednesday as an El Nino scare deepened market concern over looming dry weather through the Australian winter and spring.
Only one futures contract sold, market leader January 1998, which firmed by 50 cents to A$175.00 on the single lot sold compared with the previous settlement close.
Five A$180.00 January call options also sold at A$11.10.
Futures contract settlement prices rose across the board, with near-term contracts up by about A$1.00 a tonne and more distant contracts generally rising by A$3.00 a tonne.
Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said sellers would not meet bids of A$175.00 for the January contract and trading was ultimately confined to end user hedging.
"It's all based on the El Nino scare," he said.
